title: The Moves
corpus_scope: ICLR 2018–2026 · 67,290 author–reviewer exchanges with observable outcomes
question: What do authors do in their replies, and which of it actually moves a reviewer's judgment?

figures.title: The currency is effort
figures.deck: Softening doubles across reply-length deciles, 4.6% → 9.6% — no single move tracks softening as strongly as sheer volume of engagement.

claims.derivation: softening share of exchanges in the first vs. last decile of author reply length (median words), MOVES.effort array

figures.title: The seven moves, effort held fixed
figures.deck: One move survives the length control: the contest. "We respectfully disagree" keeps a +1.4 to +2.8pp softening premium in every reply-length stratum; every other move's premium touches or crosses zero.

claims.statement: Only 6% of the 67,290 author-reply/reviewer-response exchanges show the reviewer softening — that is the baseline every move has to beat.
claims.derivation: soft_base = 0.0597 = 5.97% ≈ 6% of the 67,290 author-reply/reviewer-response exchange pairs where the reviewer's post-response judgment softened or reversed

claims.statement: One move survives the length control: the contest keeps a +1.4 to +2.8pp softening premium in every reply-length stratum; every other move's premium touches or crosses zero.
claims.derivation: softening-rate premium of the 'disagree' (contest) move computed inside reply-length quartiles, MOVES.moves[key='disagree']; detected in 5% of exchanges

claims.statement: The delivered experiment — the move authors invest most in — is the flattest of all: within ±0.7pp of the line, negative in three of four strata, and the most negative average premium of the seven moves (−0.27pp; the ritual thanks −0.03pp and the plain revision −0.11pp also average below zero).
claims.derivation: mean of moves[key].delta_by_quartile_all over the four effort quartiles, for each of the seven moves; new_evidence is the minimum. An earlier wording claimed it was the ONLY move below zero; gratitude and revision are also below zero, and the claim was corrected 2026-08-26.
claims.verified: claim recomputed from source island; superlative corrected, 2026-08-26

caveats.text: Authors choose which move to make — a contest is deployed when the author already holds a strong hand — so a move's association with softening is not proof the move itself changes minds; a reviewer already inclined to reconsider may also be the one who draws a longer, more contested reply.

The outcome measure is conservative: it counts only judgment changes the reviewer put in writing. A reviewer who quietly raises a score without re-engaging the argument is invisible to this plate; the corpus keeps no rating history.
caveats.scope: the 67,290-exchange softening baseline and the delivered-experiment finding
